as_told.title: Plutarch names Sonchis, elder priest of the Temple of Sais, as Solon's source for the Atlantis story

plain: The ancient Greek writer Plutarch is said to name a particular elder priest, Sonchis, at the Temple of Sais in Egypt. A researcher named Matt LaCroix tells this twice in the same episode, drawing on Plutarch's Lives. The first time he simply says Plutarch describes "a very specific elder priest" at the temple named Sonchis. The second time he goes further: Sonchis was the one who "had all the knowledge," the other priests supported him, and he was the source who passed the story of Atlantis, a lost island civilization, to the Athenian lawmaker Solon, whose account the philosopher Plato later wrote down. No other teller adds to it. If true, the Atlantis story would trace back to a named, real person rather than a vague legend.
